title: JWT Authentication and Resource Servers
summary: Validate bearer access tokens with trusted keys, issuer, audience and request permissions.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Complete JWT Authentication and Authorisation in Spring Boot

richText: A JWT is a token format. A signed JWT contains a header, payload and signature. Claims are named values in the payload. Encoding does not hide the payload. Do not put passwords or private journal content in it.
A bearer token grants access to whoever holds it. Send it over HTTPS in the Authorization: Bearer header. Avoid token values in URLs or logs.
An authorization server issues an access token. A resource server is the API that accepts and validates it. Configuring a resource server does not create a login endpoint or issue tokens.

Validate the signature using trusted keys and allowed algorithms. Check issuer (iss), intended audience (aud), expiration (exp), and not-before time (nbf) when present. Decoding the payload is not validation.
For Spring Boot 3, add spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server. Configure the trusted provider’s issuer-uri. Provider metadata lets the decoder find its public keys.
The filter reads the bearer token. JwtDecoder verifies and validates it. Spring creates JwtAuthenticationToken and stores authentication for this request. Request rules then check its authorities.
By default, scopes become authorities such as SCOPE_journal.read. hasRole("USER") does not match this authority. Configure a converter explicitly if the provider has a separate roles claim.
Enforce the expected audience with a Jwt validator, or a supported Boot audiences property. issuer-uri does not by itself express which API the token is intended for.

This example leaves CSRF enabled. A read-only GET request needs no CSRF token. Before disabling CSRF for writes, ensure authentication relies only on bearer headers that browsers do not send automatically. Cookies or browser-cached Basic credentials change this decision.
Stateless means Spring does not persist this authentication in an HTTP session. An API can still call databases, caches and other services.

A valid signature does not revoke a stolen token. Choose short access-token lifetimes and an explicit revocation or refresh policy. Opaque tokens with introspection are an alternative when central validity checks are needed.

The tutorial source uses a custom filter and signing utility. It loads roles from the database on requests. Its expiration expression is one hour, despite a five-minute comment. These implementation details are separate from JWT’s general rules.
